book.definition: A set of written, printed, or digital pages bound together as a literary work.
book.example: He opened the antique leather book with reverence.

read.definition: To look at and comprehend the meaning of written characters or symbols.
read.example: She loves to read historical epics under the warm lamp.

page.definition: One side of a leaf of paper or a single rendered screen view.
page.example: He turned the page with a gentle swipe gesture.

fold.definition: To bend a surface double; the mechanical hinge of a dual-screen phone.
fold.example: The reader splits typography smoothly across the fold.

chapter.definition: One of the main structural divisions of a book or serialization.
chapter.example: The opening chapter introduced the philosophical dilemma.

story.definition: An account of imaginary or real events told for entertainment and meaning.
story.example: Every hero has an origin story etched into folklore.

knowledge.definition: Facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education.
knowledge.example: Books are ancient portals of collective human knowledge.

word.definition: A single distinct element of language carrying meaning.
word.example: Every chosen word carries resonance in poetic prose.

light.definition: Visible electromagnetic radiation that illuminates surfaces and screens.
light.example: Adjusting ambient light enhances screen contrast.

journey.definition: An act of traveling from one place to another; personal transformation.
journey.example: Every reading experience is an inward philosophical journey.

war.definition: A state of armed conflict between different nations or states.
war.example: The Art of War discusses strategic military deception.

peace.definition: Freedom from disturbance; tranquility or harmonious existence.
peace.example: True peace begins with inner serenity.

mind.definition: The faculty of consciousness, intellect, perception, and memory.
mind.example: Books are portals that expand the boundaries of the human mind.

courage.definition: The mental strength to face fear, pain, danger, or adversity.
courage.example: It took immense courage to challenge the authoritarian dogma.

freedom.definition: The power or right to act, speak, or think without hindrance or restraint.
freedom.example: The narrative celebrated human freedom above automated control.

world.definition: The setting, cosmos, or imaginative reality encompassing a literary universe.
world.example: The science fiction author built a breathtaking futuristic world.

time.definition: The continuous non-spatial continuum in which events occur sequentially.
time.example: The nonlinear narrative weaves between past and present time.

dream.definition: A series of thoughts, images, or aspirational visions of future possibility.
dream.example: He held onto his dream of exploring uncharted galaxies.

truth.definition: The quality of being in accordance with fact, reality, or moral honesty.
truth.example: Philosophy relentlessly questions appearances in search of truth.

art.definition: The expression of human creative skill, imagination, and aesthetic beauty.
art.example: Sequential comic art tells stories through expressive illustrations.

library.definition: A curated collection of books, manuscripts, and digital publications.
library.example: The digital library synchronized seamlessly across all dual-screen devices.

comic.definition: A visual storytelling medium expressing narratives through sequential art panels.
comic.example: The comic featured dynamic panel layouts across the fold.

manga.definition: Japanese comics typically read from right to left in monochrome artwork.
manga.example: He set the reader to right-to-left mode for authentic manga reading.

author.definition: The creator or writer of an original literary or scientific work.
author.example: The author crafted rich philosophical themes throughout the saga.

novel.definition: A fictional prose narrative of considerable length and complexity.
novel.example: The dystopian novel captivated readers across centuries.

screen.definition: The display surface of a monitor, tablet, or foldable mobile device.
screen.example: The anti-glare screen provided paper-like contrast.

hinge.definition: A movable joint mechanism connecting the two screens of a foldable phone.
hinge.example: The hinge sensor automatically activates dual-page reading mode.

zoom.definition: To magnify or scale an image or text view dynamically.
zoom.example: Use pinch gestures to zoom into intricate comic artwork.

gesture.definition: A movement of the fingers or hand on a touchscreen to execute commands.
gesture.example: A fast swipe gesture flips to the next comic page.

font.definition: A complete set of characters in a specific typeface design and weight.
font.example: He selected Bookerly for comfortable long-form reading.

theme.definition: A coordinated aesthetic color scheme such as Dark, Sepia, or AMOLED.
theme.example: The Sepia theme reduces blue light exposure during evening reading.

dark.definition: The absence of light; dark mode user interface reducing glare.
dark.example: Reading in dark mode conserves power on OLED displays.

note.definition: A concise textual annotation or personal observation saved during reading.
note.example: She highlighted the quote and pinned a thoughtful note.

write.definition: To compose and transcribe words or ideas into written form.
write.example: Great novelists write with profound insight into human nature.

voice.definition: The distinctive stylistic persona and tone of a narrator or character.
voice.example: The protagonist narrates the tale in a reflective first-person voice.

hero.definition: A central character admired for courage, outstanding achievements, or noble qualities.
hero.example: The hero confronted unimaginable odds to protect his realm.

villain.definition: A character whose evil actions or motives drive the central conflict of the plot.
villain.example: The villain possessed complex motives that challenged simple morality.

plot.definition: The sequence of interwoven events and turning points forming a story.
plot.example: The unexpected plot twist left readers stunned at the climax.

dialogue.definition: Conversation between two or more characters in a literary or dramatic work.
dialogue.example: Sharp, authentic dialogue revealed the underlying tensions.

thought.definition: An idea, opinion, or mental contemplation produced by thinking.
thought.example: A solitary thought sparked a profound journey of discovery.

hope.definition: A feeling of expectation and desire for a certain thing to happen.
hope.example: Hope remained the enduring beacon in the darkest hour of the tale.

wisdom.definition: The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment.
wisdom.example: The aged mentor spoke with gentle and enduring wisdom.

search.definition: To look thoroughly in an effort to find a word, book, or concept.
search.example: Search the offline dictionary for instant cross-language translations.

sync.definition: To coordinate and match data across multiple devices or repositories.
sync.example: The pull button allows users to sync all dictionaries from the repository.

open.definition: To cause to cease being closed; to launch or begin viewing a book.
open.example: Open your favorite graphic novel in dual-page view.

close.definition: To shut or exit the active book viewer and return to the library.
close.example: Swipe down from the top edge to close the active book.

bookmark.definition: A digital marker placed on a page to mark reading progress for future return.
bookmark.example: She saved a bookmark on page 245 of the manga.

share.definition: To export or transmit reading notes and quotes to another device or user.
share.example: You can export reading progress and share quotes seamlessly.

download.definition: To transfer digital files or dictionary updates from a remote repository.
download.example: Download pre-indexed dictionary packs for offline reading journeys.

save.definition: To preserve digital book files and reader settings in local device storage.
save.example: Progress is saved automatically in local IndexedDB storage.

delete.definition: To remove a book or note permanently from the local device library.
delete.example: You can delete finished books to reclaim internal flash storage.

listen.definition: To attend closely with ears; text-to-speech accessibility for audiobooks.
listen.example: Listen to narrated classics during your daily transit.

resilience.definition: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness and endurance.
resilience.example: The hero exhibited profound resilience in the face of despair.

ephemeral.definition: Lasting for a very short time; fleeting and momentary.
ephemeral.example: The sunset painted an ephemeral glow across the open pages.
